questions.question: What type of variable is shared among all instances of a class?
questions.explanation: Class variables are shared by all objects of that class.

questions.question: What type of variable is unique to each object instance?
questions.explanation: Instance variables hold data specific to each object.

questions.question: What type of method can be called without creating an instance?
questions.explanation: Static methods belong to the class rather than instances.

questions.question: What is the implicit first parameter in Python instance methods?
questions.explanation: Self refers to the instance calling the method.

questions.question: What is the implicit first parameter in Java instance methods?
questions.explanation: This keyword references the current object instance.

questions.question: What principle bundles data and methods while restricting access?
questions.explanation: Encapsulation is one of the four main OOP principles along with inheritance, polymorphism, and abstraction.

questions.question: What mechanism allows a class to acquire properties from another class?
questions.explanation: Inheritance enables code reuse by extending existing classes.

questions.question: What allows objects of different classes to be treated uniformly?
questions.explanation: Polymorphism enables a single interface to represent different types.

questions.question: What principle hides internal implementation details?
questions.explanation: Encapsulation bundles data and methods while restricting access.

questions.question: What focuses on essential features while hiding complexity?
questions.explanation: Abstraction simplifies complex systems by exposing only relevant details.

questions.question: What mechanism lets a program inspect an object's type and members at runtime?
questions.explanation: Reflection allows examining and manipulating classes and objects during execution.

questions.question: What Java method returns a string representation of an object?
questions.explanation: The toString() method, inherited from Object, produces a textual representation.

questions.question: Which Python dunder method controls what print() outputs for an object?
questions.explanation: Python calls __str__ when converting an object to a human-readable string.

questions.question: What automatic process frees memory occupied by unreferenced objects?
questions.explanation: Garbage collectors reclaim heap memory used by unreachable objects.

questions.question: What is it called when two references point to the same object?
questions.explanation: Aliasing means multiple names refer to one object, so changes are visible through both.
